overall: Los Angeles is currently running at a 71.6°F observed max as of 15:45 ET, already slightly above the NWS daytime high forecast of ~71°F. Temperatures are still rising with a positive velocity of +1.7°F/hr under broken overcast skies (BKN, ceiling ~549m), suggesting the true daily peak has not yet been reached despite the timing model flagging a local max around 15:25 ET. Marine influence remains strong with southwest winds, patchy fog potential, and sustained cloud cover keeping a lid on warming.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is wide: HRRR (72.1°F) and GFS (71.0°F) align reasonably with observations, while ECMWF (68.6°F) and NBM (67.2°F) are running well cold and appear to have underforecast today's warming. NWP peak-timing consensus points to ~16.8h ET, meaning roughly 1+ hours of potential additional warming remain from the 15:45 observation window, which supports a final TMAX above the current running max of 71.6°F.
max_temp_prediction: Given the current running max of 71.6°F with still-positive warming velocity and NWP models placing the peak at ~16-18h ET, today's TMAX is most likely to settle in the 72–73°F range. The META model (most reliable fused signal) assigns 49.2% probability to the 72–73F bucket and 23.3% each to 70–71F and 74–75F, which is coherent with the obs trajectory. Confidence is moderate — broken cloud cover and marine layer could cap further gains, but the HRRR's 72.1°F target and sustained positive velocity make a final high near 72.5°F the best central estimate.
